paragraph: Wood-Ridge is a two-tier market, and the surprise is that townhouses and condos sit above houses. Single-family closed 20 sales over six months at a median of $699,500, with a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, 45 percent of homes going above asking, and a median 27.5 days on market. That is competitive but not frenzied, and well-priced homes are moving. The typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial or cape with two full baths, and the range runs from $430,000 to $935,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Condos and townhouses, by contrast, are the volume here with 31 sales at a median of $730,000, and 26 of those 31 were townhouses, largely newer construction, which is why the tier prices above detached houses in this town. Nearly 65 percent went above asking at a median 24 days, so expect competition on the good ones. Monthly counts are thin on the single-family side, but condo closings built steadily into summer and peaked in July at eight, with the July median easing to $647,000 on higher volume. That reads as mix, not falling values. If you follow the usual seasonal arc, expect closings to taper modestly through fall before deep winter thins out. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance, newer-construction townhouse.
